title: The Surprising Mathematics of Longest Increasing Subsequences
author: Dan Romik
version: Author manuscript20 August2014; book published Cambridge2015

theorems.statement: For unit-rate exponential corner growth from the empty Young diagram, for each fixed0<epsilon<1, Pr((1-epsilon)tD subset set(Lambda(t)) subset (1+epsilon)tD) tends to1, where D={(x,y)>=0:sqrt(x)+sqrt(y)<=1}.
The embedded discrete process chooses each addable corner uniformly. Its n-cell diagram, divided by sqrt(n), converges in the two-sided dilation-inclusion sense to sqrt(6)D.

independently_proved_application: Every example factor; exponential-clock equivalence and nonexplosion; area1/6; deterministic-time sandwich; row count; uniform square-root boundary including both axes and discrete row endpoints.
external_dependency: The deep analytical proof of the continuous limit-shape theorem in sections4.3–4.6 is cited with verified hypotheses and is not claimed as independently rederived.

author_errata.assessment: Read all three pages. The chapter4 correction concerns p251 and does not change Theorems4.1 or4.5.

taocp_known_addition: all3-pre, p614 answer40,6 April2014: adds Romik Chapter4. First-edition former exercise39 is the same corner-growth problem.
bibliography_skips: The complete Rost1981 paper was not independently reread; the author-hosted Romik formulation is the explicit theorem source.
